# Results — Study 341 (MLP-Pipelines) on the real monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Three MLP "income" ETFs — the
category bellwether **AMLP** (Alerian MLP ETF), **MLPA** (Global X MLP & Energy Infrastructure)
and the leveraged **AMZA** (InfraCap MLP) — regressed on the energy sector (XLE), raced against
**SPY total return** and **XLE total return**, and decomposed into a **price** (NAV) leg and a
**return-of-capital** share. All returns are **total return** (distributions reinvested, fund
fees already inside) unless a row says "price". As-of **2026-05-31** (the partial June-2026 month
is dropped); match the per-panel fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Panel | Window | Months | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| Total-return panel (6 tickers) | 1993-02-28 → 2026-05-31 | 401 | `328f05124cbf` |
| Split-only price + distribution | 2010-08-31 → 2026-05-31 | 190 | `14b756f9af86` |

(Each fund enters only over its own listed history — AMLP from 2010-08, MLPA from 2012-04, AMZA
from 2014-10.)

## The energy beta — MLP fund regressed on XLE total return (the Signal)

| Fund | n (mo) | Energy beta (XLE) | HAC *t* | R² | Boot 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **AMLP** | 189 | **0.74** | **+5.26** | 0.64 | [0.49, 0.97] |
| **MLPA** | 169 | **0.78** | **+5.19** | 0.65 | [0.53, 1.02] |
| **AMZA** | 139 | **1.14** | **+5.46** | 0.68 | [0.74, 1.48] |

- **The "fee-based, oil-insensitive income" claim is decisively false.** Every fund loads on the
  energy sector with a HAC *t* above **5**, a bootstrap CI wholly above zero, and energy alone
  explaining 64–68% of monthly variance. AMLP is ~0.74-beta to energy; the leveraged AMZA is
  >1-beta. **This is the robust signal — and it is the opposite of the bond-like pitch.**

## The race — MLP fund vs SPY and vs XLE total return

| Fund | vs | n (mo) | Fund CAGR | Bench CAGR | Spread | HAC *t* | Fund Sharpe | Bench Sharpe | Fund maxDD | Bench maxDD |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **AMLP** | SPY | 189 | 5.3% | 15.4% | **−7.7%/yr** | −1.47 | 0.34 | 1.06 | **−73%** | −24% |
| **AMLP** | XLE | 189 | 5.3% | 8.7% | −3.8%/yr | −0.91 | 0.34 | 0.44 | −73% | −65% |
| **MLPA** | SPY | 169 | 3.8% | 14.7% | −8.3%/yr | −1.45 | 0.28 | 1.03 | −72% | −24% |
| **AMZA** | SPY | 139 | −0.8% | 14.0% | −6.6%/yr | −0.69 | 0.20 | 0.94 | **−88%** | −24% |

- **AMLP trails the market by ~8%/yr and even the energy sector by ~4%/yr,** at roughly a third of
  the market's Sharpe. The spread *t*-stats are **sub-2** on these single funds (monthly equity-like
  vol over a 12–16-year window), so the *underperformance*, while economically large, is not by
  itself robustly distinguishable — **we stamp the Signal on the energy beta (*t* > 5), not on the
  spread.**
- **The drawdown is the headline for a "bond-like" sleeve.** AMLP lost **−73%** peak-to-trough
  (the 2014–16 and 2020 oil busts) — *deeper than the energy sector's own −65%* and three times the
  market's −24%. AMZA lost −88%. This is the opposite of bond-like.

## The income illusion — distribution vs NAV (return of capital)

Split-only (price not adjusted for dividends) so the distribution is separated from NAV:

| Fund | Distribution yield | Price-NAV CAGR | Total CAGR | Return-of-capital share |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **AMLP** | 7.8%/yr | **−2.3%** | 5.4% | **1.00** |
| **MLPA** | 7.9%/yr | **−3.8%** | 3.9% | **1.00** |
| **AMZA** | 14.3%/yr | **−13.4%** | −0.7% | **1.00** |

- **The "income" is 100% your own capital handed back.** For all three the return-of-capital share
  is **1.00**: the NAV *fell* while the funds paid high distributions, so 100% of the distribution
  was financed by shrinking principal. AMZA paid a 14.3% "yield" while its NAV bled −13.4%/yr to a
  *negative* total return — a capital-destruction machine wearing an income label.

## Honest controls — the synthetic MLP replicator (offline machinery proof)

A deterministic monthly replicator (price = β·energy + NAV-bleed, plus a steady distribution)
confirms the energy-beta detector recovers the planted slope and reads ~0 on the null:

| Synthetic world | Planted beta | Recovered beta | HAC *t* | ROC share |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Positive control (β 1.10, dist 0.65%/mo, bleed −0.35%/mo) | 1.10 | ~1.08 | **> 2** | 1.00 |
| Null (β 0, no dist, no drift → flat fund) | 0.00 | ~0.00 | ~0 | n/a |

The synthetic is a *machinery proof only* — it shows the harness can detect a leveraged,
return-of-capital MLP and reads flat on the null. It never backs the Signal stamp; the real-tape
energy-beta HAC *t* above does.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** On the real tape AMLP's energy beta to XLE is 0.74 with HAC *t* = +5.26 (CI
  wholly above zero, R² 0.64), and the distribution is 100% return of capital. What's
  statistically real is the *opposite* of the pitch: a leveraged energy bet that hands back your
  own NAV as "income".
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** As a "bond-like income" sleeve it is strictly worse than the thing it
  is sold against: a −73% drawdown (deeper than energy itself), a third of the market's Sharpe, and
  a self-financed yield. A worse bond *and* a worse stock.
- **"Fat-yield free lunch"? — BUSTED.** The marketed promise (high, stable, oil-insensitive,
  bond-like income) is rejected on every hypothesis: H₁ (low energy beta), H₂ (yield not return of
  capital), H₃ (bond-like risk) and H₄ (matches the market with yield on top) all fail.
